campaign.title: Aurelia 1978 launch campaign and Logix Computer Academy
campaign.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.
message: Logix Aurelia—a computer like no other. Your personal assistant in business.
Learn before you decide.
Business Tools organise office work; Abacus supports planning; independent BPI Systems maintains business records. Logix supplies the computer, not ownership of every application.
audience: Nontechnical business owners and managers; secondary audiences are dealers, software developers and peripheral manufacturers.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify the demonstrations, operating limits and public commitments.

marketing_presentation.description: Qualify 500-plus-row workload with stated RAM, populated-cell/formula count, IF and fill-down semantics, measured recalculation and disk loading time; sparse storage is not proof of performance.
Qualify powered-on attachment at quiescent ports, including electrical sequencing and safe suspension of keyboard polling; no unplugging during printing or disk writes.
Demonstrate save/close/reopen without loss; printer, disk and projection paths must pass the complete rehearsal.
Confirm celebrity/partner contracts, venue, Academy cities/course dates, product packages, delivery, warranty and service before publishing definitive claims.
Measured 48 KB workspace, disk capacity and supported disk configuration; 64 KB or extra drives only when qualified.
Posting consistency, correction history, disk-full handling and tested backup/restore.
Readable reports on launch display and supported printers; supported forms and paper documented.
Payroll jurisdictions, update process and maintenance responsibility explicitly documented.
Qualify BPI summary export and Abacus import; demonstrate actual sequential applications and label prepared data.

marketing_steps.description: Invite business customers to the Aurelia premiere and demonstrations.

marketing_presentation.description: The proposed advertisement is a {duration_seconds}-second film trailer, with {lead} proposed as its lead. In the final {reveal_seconds} seconds, show Aurelia, Abacus, a printed result, the logo and the June 5 premiere date. Include a recognisable, independently branded BPI report; explain accounting in print and follow-up films. Casting remains subject to contract.

Narrator introduces This spring. Douglas discusses a remarkably helpful new assistant during a therapy session. The reveal identifies Aurelia as a computer, and the therapist becomes curious about a demonstration. Warm humour, concrete business benefits and consistent interaction; avoid unhealthy dependency or claims of speech recognition/artificial intelligence. Telephone enquiries, mailed brochures, demo appointments and Academy bookings; trained staff handle responses.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Aurelia as a business assistant at NCC on 5 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter} introduces almost four years of development toward an accessible, dependable business assistant; acknowledges the assembled personal computers popularised in 1977.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Reveal one Aurelia platform with detachable keyboard and two display choices. Power on colour and 16-shade grayscale systems and show startup; no claim of two different CPU models.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Prepare a customer quotation letter, demonstrate consistent editing and the copy-buffer; explain how learning transfers between applications.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Attach the self-powered printer at a safely quiescent FlexiBUS port with Aurelia powered on, wait for identification, and print. Once the job finishes, safely interchange printer and keyboard ports and verify both. No removal during traffic or unrestricted hot-plug claim.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Use address book, calendar and calculator in the same customer-order workflow.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Safely attach external FDD, load Abacus from diskette, explain a small worksheet, then open a 500-plus-row business document. Raise supplier costs by 8%, show automatic recalculation, add and fill a column using IF to flag low-margin orders, print a short report, save, close and reopen. Use readable worksheet sections on 320x200 launch displays. Use a labelled prepared worksheet with BPI-exported totals; explain their origin. The separate BPI session on 6 June shows the source records and export. Rehearse the shorter slot; retain the full workload for hands-on sessions.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Gary explains independent CP/M OEM availability, published interfaces and optional extensions; CP/M, hardware and application licenses remain distinct. MPI explains the printer partnership and any separately agreed future FlexiBUS devices. Do not announce the later July SMC agreement. The head of BPI Systems explains its independent brand, management, software ownership and support, with {presenter}’s investment, AION/Logix cooperation and AION’s C/TUI redevelopment commitments disclosed. No invented name or claim of unrelated ownership.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Announce Logix Computer Academy in five US cities: learn before you decide, hands-on Fundamentals, configuration advice and direct ordering. Show selected locations, first course dates once finalised. BPI-authorised courses and the dealer programme start July 17; specialist support is provided by BPI.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. State complete package contents, delivery dates, warranty, training and service; invite orders, Academy registration and dealer demonstrations; announce the two technical sessions. Show optional dealer-assembled BPI configurations, separate supplier licences and training and setup arrangements.
Booked auditorium or negotiated NCC presentation slot in Anaheim; access to a main stage is not assumed.
Moderated questions follow the presentation.
Colour and grayscale launch monitor options; readable 320x200 worksheet sections, not an implied 80-column or whole-document display.

marketing_steps.description: Explain Aurelia architecture and third-party peripheral development.

marketing_presentation.description: FlexiBUS, display interfaces, implementation/licensing, compatibility and third-party peripheral development.

marketing_steps.description: Demonstrate the Aurelia development environment and SDK.

marketing_presentation.description: Build and run an application, common TUI behaviour, published interfaces and C source portability without promising universal binary compatibility.

Demonstrate qualified AION C IDE editing, optimizing compilation, C/assembly library linkage and calls into the shared ROM TUI. State actual RAM/disk requirements; shared source/API contracts do not imply universal binary compatibility or an already released future target.

Demonstrate syntax highlighting and diagnostic navigation, qualified optimization profiles, an assembly library and a keyboard-operated form with bounded data controls. Show text/bitmap presentation only on tested modes; identify SDK composite helpers separately from native ROM services and publish measured resource/performance results.

marketing_steps.description: Present the independent BPI business applications on 6 June 1978.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Independent BPI Systems demonstrates a small wholesaler: existing customer/invoice records, incoming payment and remaining balance, receivables/payables and a concise report, then summary export for Abacus. Prepared history is labelled. No live write-back or simultaneous applications. Software presenter explains the workflow; the BPI head speaks in this dedicated session.
{provider} covers setup, payments, corrections, backups, month-end, inventory and payroll coverage.

marketing_steps.description: Turn initial interest into informed configuration choices and supported training.

marketing_presentation.description: The Academy was established on {established_date} and is announced publicly on {announcement_date}. Launch in {city_count} US cities with a {fundamentals_days}-day Fundamentals course. Small classes, substantial hands-on time, ideally one machine per participant or pair; business tools, introductory Abacus and advice on appropriate configurations and unnecessary purchases. Order and pay at training centres; immediate collection only where stock is available. No purchase obligation.
BPI-authorised training starts on {start_date}. Access to a BPI specialist at each launch centre; authorised curriculum and escalation agreement. Training, setup and software licensing are separate.

marketing_steps.description: Make the NCC programme available for television coverage.

marketing_presentation.description: Every Logix presentation at NCC 1978, including the premiere, both technical sessions, partner appearances, questions and any additional Logix sessions. Offer and supply the material to any television station wishing to broadcast it; Logix arranges normal duplication and dispatch. Supply station-compatible broadcast copies on request.

campaign.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
campaign.objective: Encourage independent manufacturers and developers to adopt documented compatibility interfaces, and show customers how supported software, documents and peripherals can protect their investment across computer brands.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Use documented interfaces and qualified configurations to connect products from independent suppliers.
Choose CP/M applications, FlexiBUS peripherals and display options separately; adopting one does not require the entire Logix platform.
Prepare for future computers through portable C source and documented interfaces while continuing to use and support established eight-bit systems.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify partner claims and protect the next-generation architecture disclosure.

marketing_presentation.description: Identify shipping products, qualified configurations, prototypes and plans separately. Manufacturer interest and campaign targets are not signed agreements, verified adoption or sales.

CP/M remains commercially licensed. Non-exclusive implementation rights do not change software ownership or imply open-source licensing. Reference-code rights, certification scope and support terms must be stated before making firm offers.
Claim compatibility only for named software versions, resources, host adapters and tested configurations. Preserve each supplier’s brand, licences and support responsibilities.
Label the Model II demonstration as a prototype until customer release. AION supplies the June 1979 cards; SMC remains a future source subject to individual chip qualification.

Apple’s demonstration participation covers native Apple II products and does not endorse S-100 systems. These products provide neither Apple CP/M/Z80 execution nor automatic conversion of existing Apple graphics.

Until 19 May 1980, refer to future systems only as next-generation computers. Withhold product, processor and OS names; word size, ISA, registers, execution design, address and memory organisation; performance figures, clock rates, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology and future display specifications.

Keep coprocessor implementation and integration details, future-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries and revealing benchmarks confidential. Apply this embargo to presentations, questions, advertising, dealer scripts, sales proposals, OEM briefings, clinics and all attachments; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional display documentation may be shared.

Use released eight-bit software and explicitly identified qualified prototypes in demonstrations. Label prepared data and recordings, obtain partner clearance, and report measured resource and interoperability limits rather than implying universal performance.
Do not imply an engineering guarantee, product withdrawal date or promise that every model remains in production. Do not promise funded support for an unspecified duration.

marketing_steps.description: Demonstrate independent customer choices at NCC 1979.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {programme_minutes} minutes for the presentation programme; questions and follow-up are separate.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Explain how independent software, peripheral and display choices can protect a customer’s investment.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the Model II prototype using separately qualified host editions. Show supported common behaviour without promising identical binaries or disk formats.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate Abacus, then independent BPI records and summary export. Explain the prepared data and separate licensing; do not imply that BPI has a Model II port.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Operate a qualified peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, driver support and supported application functions, attaching only when the port is quiescent.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Present the Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II alongside the S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. An Apple representative joins the native Apple demonstration. Explain the drivers, optional display hardware and separate S-100 support without suggesting Apple endorses S-100 systems.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. DRI, Tandy, Microsoft, BPI management and confirmed peripheral participants explain their responsibilities and commercial access. Distinguish current AION chip supply from prospective SMC supply and signed partners from recruitment prospects.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter} explains that future computers will not run existing Z80 binaries natively. Existing C tools and documented APIs reduce source migration work; recompilation, adaptation and testing remain necessary. Describe the planned optional Z80 coprocessor and the continuing role of eight-bit systems without revealing the new architecture.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Identify available products, prototypes and future plans. Direct customers and developers to documented configurations, licence terms, the compatibility directory and programme registration.

marketing_steps.description: Explain the separate software, peripheral and display compatibility profiles.

marketing_presentation.description: Specify the CP/M core and optional extension versions, processor instruction set, available transient-program memory, adapters and qualified applications for each configuration. Document common file formats and APIs. FlexiBUS and Logix video are optional; native displays, disks and conventional ports remain valid. Ordinary CP/M support does not guarantee every extended application, Z80 binary, file system or floppy format.

Publish electrical and transport rules, device-class profiles, host drivers, diagnostics and named qualification results. Other processors and operating systems may use their own drivers without adopting CP/M or Logix video. Device identification alone does not prove feature compatibility. Version 1 uses one device per point-to-point port, with no passive hub or daisy chain; its faster rate allows at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.

Separate graphics API compatibility from controller cards, the digital monitor link and qualified display modes. FlexiBUS and the full Aurelia architecture are optional. An 80-column mode needs a qualified 640-pixel monitor; adding a card does not give existing 320-pixel launch monitors that resolution.

The NCC launch covers the Apple II Expansion Card, FlexiDisk II, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. The Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II are existing products presented alongside the three new interface/video cards. Cards initially use AION chips and include native Apple drivers and examples or supported S-100 CP/M adapters as appropriate. Keep host requirements and supplier support explicit.
Explain implementation and qualification requirements for {subject}.
Explain supported interaction behaviour under {subject}.
Present {subject} to developers implementing supported interfaces.
Explain source portability through {subject}, with recompilation and testing still required.
Distinguish graphics API compatibility under {subject} from qualified display hardware.
Explain the qualified monitor connection defined by {subject}; this is not a consumer television interface.

marketing_steps.description: Recruit independent implementers under explicit terms and governance.

marketing_presentation.description: Describe DRI’s software leadership and Logix’s hardware contribution. Invite independent computer, peripheral and software suppliers to a programme offering published specifications, versioning, backward-support policies, reference drivers, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. Explain non-exclusive own-brand implementation, equal access to qualified components, disclosed supply priorities and manufacturer representation in a working group.

Identify the unresolved licence terms, reference-code redistribution rights, support duration and staffing, legacy-maintenance budget, working-group charter and voting rules, certification operator and scope, supply allocations, lead times and warranties. Present these as matters to settle, not existing contractual guarantees.

Invite suppliers to offer wider carriage, letter-quality printing, specialist forms and faster devices. Require the relevant status, character or graphics, paper and form-control support; the basic printer protocol does not cover every feature.
Invite business-chart and engineering-output devices, subject to a new plotting profile and suitable application support.
Invite communications and remote-access products with defined serial data, flow-control, modem-status and control profiles and host drivers.

Invite larger floppy systems, backup products and selected hard disks. Specify geometry, removable-media errors, durable writes, boot rules and measured throughput. Native faster disk controllers remain a valid choice.
Invite instruments, readers and business-input devices with published class or vendor-extension profiles and host drivers. Do not imply that foreign-processor ROM drivers execute automatically.

marketing_steps.description: Explain source migration, legacy support and the continuing eight-bit market.

marketing_presentation.description: The 4 June 1979 announcement explains source migration and the planned optional Z80 compatibility path. Full architecture disclosure is scheduled for 19 May 1980. The all-years technical catalogue is internal author material, not a 1979 press kit.

Use the established Z80 C environment, documented APIs, portable file formats and separate platform adapters. A later target needs recompilation and testing, with review of assembly code, integer and pointer assumptions, memory banking and direct hardware access. Source portability does not preserve native Z80 binary execution.

Describe an optional Z80 coprocessor planned for qualified legacy applications. Availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model or hardware-dependent program. Keep its implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration confidential until the architecture reveal.
Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development. Publish a funded support duration before making a dated service promise.
Explain that eight-bit computers retain useful business roles while falling costs broaden home, education and personal use. There is no fixed date when all business customers switch platforms.

The current professional digital monitor interface cannot drive a consumer television. A computer intended to use an existing television requires separate display engineering; the basic-storage configuration remains unresolved.

marketing_steps.description: Prepare the actual transfer demonstration, venue and architecture answers.

marketing_presentation.description: Document the actual file-transfer route and floppy formats used for the Aurelia-to-Model-II round trip. Publish tested RAM and application-workspace requirements, load and recalculation times and document-capacity limits. Label prepared data and recordings and preserve independent BPI branding and participant clearances.
Use booked presentation space; main-stage access, the exact slot and audiovisual suitability require confirmation. The eight presentation stages total 50 minutes, followed by questions.

Use this response to questions seeking confidential details: We will discuss the new architecture at NCC 1980. Today we can describe our C migration approach and planned optional Z80 compatibility path.

marketing_steps.description: Evaluate manufacturer adoption against stated targets.

marketing_presentation.description: By the end of 1979, aim for Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified third-party devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, aim for three to five distinct non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations. Count Tandy once and exclude duplicate dealer builds and product variants; these are targets, not achieved results.

campaign.objective: Communicate the launch, qualify demonstrations and coordinate follow-up described by the source campaign.
claim_policy: status: Accepted campaign plan; demonstrations and performance claims require validation

compatibility policy / scope: Released Artemis application binaries using documented, supported ERA/AIONix interfaces retain a supported execution path on subsequent Logix professional platforms through 2000: native execution, a maintained compatibility runtime, or emulation. Source portability is a separate commitment, not a substitute for the binary execution path.

compatibility policy / exclusions: Undocumented hardware access, unqualified peripherals and unsupported interfaces; no promise of unchanged speed, unlimited memory, or every future device. Z80 programs use their separately qualified compatibility path.

compatibility policy / delivery requirements: Publish versioned ABI/API eligibility and conformance tests; preserve reference binaries and regression workloads; budget compatibility engineering, runtime distribution and support. Staffing, funding and validation remain explicit launch readiness gates.
compatibility policy / status: Official scenario commitment at NCC 1980; future fulfilment is not established evidence.

claims / memory: Beyond the 64 KB application barrier; demonstrate a measured resident workload on a named 128 KB or 256 KB configuration. Finite RAM and process limits remain; no demand paging promised.

claims / os: Professional multitasking AIONix with Unix V7-inspired behaviour and familiar Logix TUI/keyboard conventions. Do not claim a Unix source licence or trademark endorsement without an established agreement.

claims / compiler: Artemis-hosted AION C IDE supplies ERA native and Z80 cross-compilers, target libraries and separate executables. Portable code following guidelines can require small changes; quantify changes for each demonstration rather than promising zero work.

claims / applications: Native Abacus 2, Business Tools and qualified independent BPI editions. Pulse 1 remains Aurelia+ software; a card demonstration requires guest OS/memory qualification. Native Pulse 3 and Abacus 3 launch only at COMDEX on November 19.
claims / continuity: Aurelia+ remains a supported value option; compatible independent 8-bit computers grow the ecosystem. No forced migration or promise that cheaper 8-bit demand disappears.

campaign.title: COMDEX 1979 campaign and presentation

message: More room to work. More freedom to choose.
Your existing software. Less waiting.
Calculate once. Chart it. Print the documents.

marketing_steps.description: Present Aurelia+, Abacus 2 and qualified partner applications at COMDEX 1979.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {programme_minutes} minutes for the presentation programme; questions and follow-up are separate.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter}: growing businesses need more capacity, less waiting and compatible choices.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Identical live calculated shaded-cube animation on Aurelia and Aurelia+, followed by identical Abacus recalculation and chart generation; present measured results. Use {explanation_minutes} minute for explanation and {animation_minutes} minutes for the live shaded cube. Calculate rotation, project vertices, determine visible faces, calculate shading and draw a fixed sequence of cube rotations live. No prerecorded animation or precomputed frames. Same executable and inputs on both machines, compatible with both Same resolution, shading method, rendering settings and equivalent qualified display configurations; disclose unavoidable differences Visible start countdown, elapsed time and completed-frame count Fixed frame/rotation sequence completes the same amount of work; no silent frame skipping or quality reduction Use a workload that fits both machines; demonstrate additional capacity separately Both machines must finish correctly; publish results only after measurement Same Abacus 2.0 executable, worksheet values/formulas, calculation settings and chart workload. Compare recalculation and chart-generation time; exclude physical printer time. Animation measures the combined calculation/display path, not pure CPU performance. The catalog clocks are 4 and 6 MHz, but no 1.5x or other application speedup is promised.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Chart employee pay values; link fields to a payslip layout; preview employees and print the entire batch. Demonstrate charts and document layouts populated by spreadsheet field values. Use the catalogued text-mode vertical or horizontal bar charts; do not imply unimplemented graphical chart types. Fictitious employees with names, departments, pay components, deductions and precalculated net pay; one row per employee. Inspect precalculated values and reconcile totals Show a payroll-cost bar chart by department Open one reusable payslip layout and identify linked spreadsheet fields Preview different employees to show field substitution Print one complete payslip per employee from the same layout Validate field mapping, missing values, numeric formatting and rounding Validate pagination and ensure every selected employee prints exactly once with the correct values Validate save/reopen and preserve spreadsheet/document contents Reconcile BPI-exported values with source totals through documented versioned disk-file exchange Abacus charts, formats and prints supplied calculations. Payroll law/rules, statutory deductions and updates belong to the payroll application or properly maintained worksheet. No direct ledger write-back or live database link. Supporting implementation advantage for useful workloads, not a permanently exclusive general technique. Promote Abacus 2.0 on both Aurelia and Aurelia+ in supported configurations. Do not imply a new computer is required.
